The second review of 1.24.31 (MAKE STATION, AI_CONTROL's duplex floats rule and two-alarm lights, AI_ACTIONS' block
grammars), on the snapshot at commit 13c4c57, by a reviewer who did not write them and did not read the first review.

  node tests/fixtures/station_review2_1231/replay.js            -> 242 cases: 175 AGREE, 67 DISAGREE
                                                                    (5 high, 30 medium, 32 low)
  node tests/fixtures/station_review2_1231/make_before.js       -> before.json (1.24.30, ad0d654: routing of every
                                                                    question here and of all 300 bench questions, and each
                                                                    cases_d circuit)
  node tests/fixtures/station_review2_1231/make_grammar.js      -> grammar_cases.json (95 grammars, 135 samples)
  python3 tools/gbnf_check.py --lib /tmp/llama/llama-b11435/libllama.so --vocab <ggml-vocab-qwen2.gguf> \
      tests/fixtures/station_review2_1231/grammar_cases.json --out tests/fixtures/station_review2_1231/grammar_results.json
                                                                 -> all 95 grammars parsed; 13 samples disagree (below)

Files: cases_a.js (MAKE STATION blocks as models write them), cases_b.js (routing, with every bench question as a
guard), cases_c.js (read as STATION; Chat and solve), cases_d.js (the duplex floats rule; two alarm lights),
cases_e.js (grammars, and when they are sent), cases_f.js (parts list, how it works, the checks, what is not known).
lib.js holds the judges: every control drawn is simulated (sim.js: lead float starts one pump, the off float stops it,
the pumps take turns over four cycles, the lag float runs both and both hold to the off float, the alarm float lights
the alarm, an overload drops only its pump); each pump's check then shutoff valve; the levels' order and heights; and
that the three drawings and the parts list name the same floats and pumps.

FINDINGS, most harm first

 1. [high] A station question that also asks for another drawing loses it (B-34, C-27; B-33, C-26 medium).
    "Draw a motor starter circuit, then the piping and the float levels of a duplex lift station": asks() is true
    (a wet well, two views named), relevant() offers MAKE STATION alone and AI_PARTS does not split, so the motor
    starter is never asked for; the station's alternator circuit stands in its place. 1.24.30 split it
    CONTROL+PIPING+LEVELS and drew the starter: a regression. Same for a picture ("Draw a house with a red roof,
    then the control circuit and piping of a duplex lift station") -- 1.24.30 lost the house too, but the whole rule
    keeps it lost. asks() looks at the whole question, and OTHER lists only other tools' nouns (slides, sheet...).
    Right: whole only when the question asks for nothing else; otherwise in parts, the station's drawings one
    STATION part (as is done for a slide deck beside them).

 2. [high] The count of pumps misread, silently (A-81, A-27b high; A-27, A-28 medium).
    "pumps one duty, one standby" -> 1 pump (the first count word): a simplex drawn, its lag float dropped with
    "one pump has no lag pump"; nothing says the count was read so. "pumps 3x 2 HP" -> 2 (the HP; "3x" is not a
    number): a duplex drawn whole for a triplex. "pumps 2x 15 HP" -> 15 pumps (the float levels only). "3 pumps"
    (number first) -> unread, and "2 pumps: the block did not say". Right: duty/standby counted in words as in
    digits (the dm pattern takes only digits); "Nx" is N; a number before "pumps" is the count; the HP never.
    (Adam's question names 2 pumps and overrules the block, so the bench does not see this.)

 3. [high] Read as STATION, the control and the levels disagree, and the text follows the levels, not the circuit
    drawn (C-08 high; C-12 medium). A duplex MAKE CONTROL (off, lead, FS3 high level alarm, no lag) beside a MAKE
    LEVELS (FS3 lag on, FS4 alarm): "How it works" says "If the water still rises to FS3 (lag on), the other pump
    starts too, and both run" -- the circuit drawn has no lag call; the checks say "Lift FS4 (high level alarm): the
    alarm light comes on" -- the control drawn has no FS4 and its alarm light is on FS3, which the parts list calls
    "Float switch: lag on". The only warning names the jobs ("alarm, lead, off; alarm, lag, lead, off"), not the
    tag. A person commissioning from it lifts the wrong float. Right: the sequence and checks from the circuit drawn
    (checks() already guards its lag line by the circuit; sequence() and the alarm lines do not), or back once
    naming the conflicting tag with the line to write.

 4. [medium] Right blocks refused or stripped by the floats line's reading (A-12, A-62, A-59; A-24, A-60, A-58,
    A-74 low). JOBRE matches "lag pump" and then "on" as a second job: "floats all pumps off 2 ft, lead pump on
    3 ft, lag pump on 4 ft, high level alarm 5 ft" goes back with "two heights for the lead on float: write it once,
    like: float FS1 \"lead on\" <its height>" (the off float's tag, and a placeholder: A-74). "pump 1 on, pump 2 on"
    -> the second merged into the lead: the lag float lost, nothing said (MAKE CONTROL's floatJob reads "pump 2 on"
    as the lag). "lag off" -> "lag" + "off", the lag pump's own off float lost. An alarm on its own line ("alarm
    high level float") is unread and the station then says "no high level alarm float: the block has none"; "low
    level alarm float 1 ft" and "high level alarm horn and light" lines unread (the station grammar lets "alarm",
    "high", "low" lines through: they are in grammarWords).

 5. [medium] Floats written tag first are not read (A-14, A-15). "FS1 off 2 ft", "FS1: off float at 2 ft" (MAKE
    LEVELS' own form, which MAKE CONTROL also reads, and which the station grammar lets through as a tag line) are
    unread: the heights the answer gave are lost and the usual floats drawn not to scale (said as unread).

 6. [medium] A float label that begins with a digit sends a right station back (A-79). float FS3 "2nd pump start"
    reaches MAKE LEVELS as float FS3 "2nd pump start", whose heightOf(line) reads `3 "` (the tag's digit and the
    quote) as 3 in; the other floats have none, so the station goes back for heights it never gave, the line
    offered giving FS3 "3 in". (AI_PUMP_STATION's parseLevels, reached through the station.)

 7. [medium] Lines sent back for heights that, copied, are sent back again (A-72, A-73; rule 3). Heights for two
    floats of four ("off 2 ft, lead, lag, alarm 5 ft"): the line gives lead and lag both 3.5 ft (each the midpoint of
    the same neighbours), which goes back again. The unit written once at the end ("off 2.0, lead 3.0, lag 4.0,
    alarm 5.0 ft"): three heights dropped silently, and back with a line that leaves them out. Right: spread the
    missing heights; read a list's trailing unit for the bare numbers, or ask for the unit with this block's numbers.

 8. [medium] The correction of a read-as-station reply names the wrong block (C-11, C-20). A right MAKE CONTROL and
    a MAKE LEVELS with its heights out of order: "Lantern checked your MAKE CONTROL block: the float levels: ...",
    with the control's guide, "Reply with the corrected block only (MAKE CONTROL: ...)", and held to the CONTROL
    grammar -- so the mended levels cannot be sent, and a reply of the control alone loses the heights. Right: name
    MAKE LEVELS (its guide, its grammar), or ask for the one MAKE STATION block.

 9. [medium] Piping of 3 pumps beside a duplex control, or alone for a 2-pump question: drawn as written while the
    station says 2 pumps ("2 pumps: the question asks for 2 (the block said 3)"); the parts list has 3 pumps, 3 check
    and 3 shutoff valves and 2 starters; nothing says the drawings disagree (C-09, C-10). sp.warn compares only the
    control's count.

10. [medium] The duplex floats rule adds a wet well's floats to things that are not pumps (D-11, D-12, D-13). An
    alternator for "the two standby generators at the lift station", "the lift station's two odor control units",
    "the two heaters in the lift station's control building": WETP matches "lift station" in the question, NOTWET
    lists compressors, fans, blowers, boilers but not these, and the coils' own labels (generator, odor unit, heater)
    are not asked. Rule 7: the coils say what they are. Right: add the floats only when the coils are pumps (a pump
    label, or none) and the pumps are a wet well's. (D-01 to D-10, D-14 to D-20 agree: lift station, sewage, storm
    water, sump, a coil named sewage; nothing added for boosters, compressors, a cooling tower, fans, pressure
    switches, a partial set of floats.)

11. [medium] The two-alarm-lights rule drops an alarm (D-24, a regression). A "lag on / alarm" float (the lag and the
    alarm in one, which AI_CONTROL draws) with a high level alarm float FS4 and "lamp LT3 FS4": 1.24.30 lit LT3 from
    either alarm float; now LT3 is FS4's only, FS3's alarm lights nothing, and nothing says so. (D-21 to D-23, D-25,
    D-26 agree: two alarms a light each, a light naming both, a light and a horn, a light naming neither.)

12. [medium] The commissioning text says what was not drawn (F-05, F-15, F-16, F-03, F-09; F-10 low).
    Two alarms and a horn: Lantern draws the horn on the high high float only, and the checks say "Lift FS4 (high
    level alarm): the alarm light and horn come on" (F-05; the horn is also labelled "high level": F-06, low).
    Read as STATION, a control whose alarm is a horn and no light: "the alarm light and horn come on" (F-16).
    A lag pump's own off float (written float FS2 "lag off"): drawn right (the lag call stops at FS2), but how it
    works says "both run until the water is down to FS1" (F-15). No alarm float, or no control drawn (three pumps,
    six): "What Lantern does not know" still says "The alarm Lantern draws is a light on the control circuit's own
    power" (UNKNOWN is fixed text) (F-03, F-09, F-10).

13. [medium] Lines that are not the control voltage become the ladder's rails (A-55; A-56, A-78 low). "power 480 V
    3 phase" (the pumps' power) -> rails "480 V 3 phase"; "voltage: 480 V 3 phase, control 120 V" -> the whole line;
    prose "Power: if the power fails the alarm dials out on a 12 V battery" -> that sentence (the grammar lets it
    through, E-GS-36). Right: a control voltage only (volts, AC or DC, not 3 phase), the part marked control when
    two are given; otherwise unread.

14. [medium] "Draw the wiring and piping of a sump pump with a backup pump" is a station of one pump ("one pump (the
    question asks for a sump pump)"): the backup pump dropped (B-44). (1.24.30 drew it as SCHEMATIC+PIPING.)

15. [medium] `inlet 8" at 6'` (inch and foot marks): the pipe's 8 in read as the invert, and the levels say three
    times, falsely, that the inlet fills before the alarm and before each pump starts (A-45). The inch-mark rule is
    applied to float lines only; "at" makes the size a height.

16. [low] Routing takes as a station what is none of its three drawings: a power one-line (B-29), the odor control
    system (B-30), a generator transfer switch's wiring (B-31); bypass pumping split STATION+PIPING (B-32).

17. [low] Station drawings asked beside another thing not made one STATION part when a part's text carries the
    other tool's word: SHEET+CONTROL+PIPING (B-39), PIPING+LEVELS with an e-mail (B-40), CONTROL+LEVELS with the quiz
    swallowed into the LEVELS part (B-41), "Design a lift station and give me a budget": only the sheet offered,
    the station lost (B-42), a flow chart (B-48). Each is as 1.24.30 had it; B-49 (a control panel: no tool) too.

18. [low] The station grammar is narrower than the parser (E-GS-leads, E-GS-layout; E-GC-04, E-GP-03 for CONTROL
    and PIPING): "shut-off valves", "wet-well", "force-main", "high-level light" (a hyphen after a grammar word:
    rest must start with space : = , .), "swing check valves", "flap check valves" (LEADS' check kinds are not in
    grammarWords, though its comment says every LEADS word is), "the wet well", a round bullet, indented lines,
    "Off float FS1" (MAKE CONTROL reads it). Each is held out by llama.cpp; harmless while the model then finds a
    spelling the parser reads. And wider: prose that begins with a line's word gets through (E-GS-36, E-GS-37).

19. [low] Grammar counted though not sent (E-s05): with a server that is not llama.cpp's, Chat's rec.grammar (and
    solve's out.grammar, counted in held()) records calls held to a grammar when callServer sent none.

20. [low] Small misreadings and lines: "wet well: 8' x 8' x 12' deep" -> 8 ft deep (A-43); "main breaker 60 A" ->
    the force main labelled "breaker 60 A force main" (A-49); a low level alarm drawn and never in the checks
    (F-07); the checks send the reader to the float levels' drawing, the valves or an alternating relay that were not
    drawn when a show line limits the drawings (F-12, F-13, F-14); bottom/middle/top floats: "top" read as the lead,
    "middle" sent back as "lag on", which copied draws the top float below the middle one (A-80); the one-pump
    control's correction line written on one line with commas ("alternator AR M1 M2, coil M1 ..."), copied as one
    line, goes back again (C-13; the same style as 1.24.30's alternator line).

What held (AGREE): the guide's forms and the ways small models vary them (capitals, colons, bullets, numbers, inch
marks, feet and inches, mixed units, metres, elevations, depths below grade, heights before jobs, jobs before tags,
ISA tags, two alarms, a low level alarm, stop/start, low/high level) -- every control drawn among them simulated
right, every pump with its check then shutoff valve, the levels in order and to scale; simplex, triplex, four and six
pumps; the bench's 300 questions routed and split exactly as 1.24.30 apart from the two lift stations (B-45, B-46);
whole-station questions, single drawings, prose questions, boosters, irrigation, chilled water, condensate, ladder
logic; STATION beside slides, a sheet, code, cards, music; read-as-station of the 35B's own control, a control, a
piping, a levels, schematics holding either, all three; Chat and solve asking once for the station (with its
grammar) after a picture, a plain starter, a sheet or prose; one correction only; all 95 kinds' grammars parsed by
llama.cpp with an empty block let through; the guide's lines, the fix hint's lines, the drawings' own blocks as
Lantern writes them, the 35B's control let through; prose before, inside or after a block, a code fence, no END, and
another kind held out; no grammar on a first call, none when the correction names another kind; a refused grammar
(400) or one that fails mid-reply (500) dropped and the request made again; the Writer document's sections and
escaping; the parts list's quantities and tags.

NOT RUN OR NOT CHECKED
 - No model was run: every reply is scripted. The grammars were checked with llama.cpp b11435's grammar sampler and
   Qwen2's vocabulary only (tokens of the sample offered one at a time), not with a Qwen3.5 model generating under
   them; what a small model writes once a line is held out is not known.
 - The kit's own llama-server version, and whether it accepts body.grammar on /v1/chat/completions as b11435 does,
   were not checked; nor the in-page (device) engine with a grammar in its options.
 - No browser run (tests/browser, review_station_1231.py): no drawing was looked at (label overlap, scale, the two
   alarm lights, the horn), nor the Writer document or the PDF.
 - The commissioning text's sources (OSHA 1910.146/147, 1926 Subpart AA, Ten States 2014, Ontario 2008, the pump
   maker's manual) were not checked against their pages (no web in this review).
 - npm test was not run; tests/station.js was run on the snapshot and passes (49).
 - The first review's fixtures (station_review1_1231) were not read, by design: some findings may repeat it.
 - sim.js holds every switch in its run position (a lead/lag selector or HOA switch is not exercised) and does not
   time anything; a station of three or more pumps has no control drawn to simulate.
 - Questions in parts were tried for two parts (one with three); longer ones, and questions not in English, were not.
